title: Approximate an fpqc scheme model by a finite type flat subcover of a Dedekind base
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $B$ be a commutative $R$-algebra such that $\operatorname{Spec}B\to S$ is flat and surjective [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Let $F:(\mathit{Sch}/S)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathit{Sets}$ be an fpqc sheaf, meaning that it satisfies the covering equalizer condition for [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Suppose the restriction $F_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$ is represented by a $\operatorname{Spec}B$-scheme $P$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-representable-functor] whose structure morphism is of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated) [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. There is a finitely generated $R$-subalgebra $C\subseteq B$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] such that $\operatorname{Spec}C\to S$ is flat, surjective and of finite presentation, and $F_{\operatorname{Spec}C}$ is represented by a $\operatorname{Spec}C$-scheme $Q$ of finite presentation. No finite-presentation hypothesis on $B/R$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation (objects, arrows and equalities), applied to the scheme and its canonical descent isomorphism and cocycle over the tensor-square and tensor-cube systems; combined with more-algebra.tex Tag 0AUW, lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat. This is the first paragraph of Anantharaman Lemma 4.2.1, printed pp.55-56, with the fpqc equalizer identification made explicit; local Anantharaman archive WANTED.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the set of finitely generated $R$-subalgebras $C$ of $B$, ordered by inclusion. It is nonempty (the image of $R$ is a stage), directed (adjoin the union of two finite generating sets), and has union $B$ (adjoin any given element). Compatible ring maps from its stages to a ring glue uniquely by evaluation on this union, so $B=\varinjlim_I C$. Put $U_C=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $U=\varprojlim_I U_C$. All transition maps are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], and all stages are affine; in particular the stages are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Work in a universe containing this set of subalgebras and the big fpqc site, with the size convention of [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Tag 01YW, lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit; the union argument is written out here

proof.text: Every $C\in I$ is already an allowable flat cover of $S$. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] makes $B$ a flat $R$-module. For $0\ne a\in R$, the injection $R\xrightarrow{a}R$ remains injective after tensoring with $B$, by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; thus multiplication by $a$ on $B$, and hence on its submodule $C$, is injective. Apply [lem-sfb-dedekind-torsionfree-module-flat] to $C$ with the given Noetherian, normal, dimension-at-most-one domain $R$, then [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] to obtain flatness of $U_C\to S$. For each prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, choose a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ over it, using surjectivity of $U\to S$. Its contraction to $C$ lies over $\mathfrak p$, so $U_C\to S$ is surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], $C$ is finitely presented over $R$. The affine presentation gives local finite presentation, and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness, so $U_C\to S$ is of finite presentation. A flat surjective map of affines is a singleton fpqc covering by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], over an affine open of its target its inverse image is affine and surjects onto that open. This applies also to $U\to S$.

source.place: Tag 0AUW, lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat (1); algebra.tex Tag 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation (3); morphisms.tex Tag 01U5, lemma-flat-characterize

proof.text: Write $D_C^{(n)}=C^{\otimes_R n}$ and $D^{(n)}=B^{\otimes_R n}$ for $n=2,3$. These tensor powers need not embed in $D^{(n)}$. Nevertheless $D^{(n)}=\varinjlim_C D_C^{(n)}$: by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], a compatible family of maps $C\otimes_R C\to E$ is exactly two compatible families of maps $C\to E$ agreeing on $R$, hence two maps $B\to E$ agreeing on $R$, hence a map $B\otimes_R B\to E$. The same argument with three maps proves the cube assertion. It holds on every tail $C\supseteq C_0$, since finite generating sets can be united with those of $C_0$. All stages $\operatorname{Spec}D_C^{(n)}$ are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and the transition maps between them are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] identifies the limits of the affine square and cube systems with $U\times_S U$ and $U\times_S U\times_S U$, respectively; the affine tensor identifications, including each projection, are [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra].

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; limits.tex Tag 01YW, with the tensor-colimit universal-property calculation written here

proof.text: Choose the given natural representation $e:h_P\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_U$. On $U\times_S U$, its pullbacks $e_1,e_2$ identify the functors of points of $p_1^*P,p_2^*P$ with the same restricted functor $F$. By [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful], $e_2^{-1}e_1$ is represented by a unique isomorphism $\delta:p_1^*P\xrightarrow{\sim}p_2^*P$ (represent the inverse too and use faithfulness). On the triple product the equations $(e_3^{-1}e_2)(e_2^{-1}e_1)=e_3^{-1}e_1$ give $\delta_{23}\delta_{12}=\delta_{13}$, again by faithfulness. These are the actual canonical descent identifications of $F$, not an arbitrarily chosen datum on $P$. Every pulled-back scheme used here is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3).

source.place: Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda, applied on each slice; the canonical cocycle is the displayed cancellation

proof.text: Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](1) to $P\to U$ and the system $(U_C)$. It gives $C_0\in I$, a scheme $Q_0$ of finite presentation over $U_{C_0}$ and a specified $U$-isomorphism $(Q_0)_U\simeq P$. For every $C\supseteq C_0$ put $Q_C=Q_0\times_{U_{C_0}}U_C$. Each $Q_C\to U_C$ is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Use these specified isomorphisms to regard $\delta$ and $\delta^{-1}$ as maps between the two pullbacks of $(Q_0)_U$.

Over $\operatorname{Spec}D_{C_0}^{(2)}$ take the two pullbacks of $Q_0$ by the two projections. They are of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Their limit pullbacks are the source and target of $\delta$. Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](2) on the square system of step 3 to $\delta$ and to $\delta^{-1}$, choosing a common larger $C_1$ by directedness. This yields maps $d_1:p_1^*Q_{C_1}\to p_2^*Q_{C_1}$ and $a_1$ in the reverse direction whose base changes to $B\otimes_R B$ are precisely $\delta$ and $\delta^{-1}$. No flatness or surjectivity of $C_1\to B$ is being asserted or used.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation (2), on the tensor-square inverse system

proof.text: The two equations $a_1d_1=\mathrm{id}$ and $d_1a_1=\mathrm{id}$ hold at the square limit. By [thm-pd-spreading-out](3), they hold at a common later square stage $C_2$. Pull $d_{C_2}$ back along the three projections from $\operatorname{Spec}D_{C_2}^{(3)}$ to its tensor-square. The maps $d_{23}d_{12}$ and $d_{13}$ have common source and target of finite presentation over that cube stage, by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Their limit maps agree by step 4. Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](3) on the cube system and enlarge to $C_3\supseteq C_2$ so that this equation holds. The inverse equations remain true after base change. Set $C=C_3$, $V=U_C$, $Q=Q_C$, and $d=d_C$. We have obtained an isomorphism $d:p_1^*Q\simeq p_2^*Q$ satisfying the triple cocycle, with its specified pullback equal to the canonical $\delta$ on $P$.

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation (3), first on squares for the inverse equations, then on cubes for the cocycle

proof.text: Use the big fpqc site of $S$ in the universe of step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], $h_Q$ on its slice over $V$ is a sheaf: compatible relative morphisms glue as scheme maps, and their composites to $V$ agree by uniqueness. The isomorphism $d$ induces a gluing isomorphism between its restrictions to $V\times_S V$, satisfying the triple cocycle. Since $V\to S$ is an fpqc cover by step 2, apply [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] to the singleton covering. It constructs an fpqc sheaf $H$ on $S$ and an isomorphism $H|_V\simeq h_Q$ whose overlap comparison is exactly $d$. This uses effective descent for set sheaves, and does not claim effective descent for arbitrary schemes.

source.place: Tag 04TR, lemma-glue-sheaves, singleton case; descent.tex Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms

proof.text: Restrict the isomorphism of step 8 along $U\to V$, and compose with the specified $Q_U\simeq P$ and $e$. It gives $b:H|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_U$. On $U\times_S U$ the two restrictions of $b$ agree: the overlap for $H$ is the pullback of $d$, namely $\delta$, and $e_2\delta=e_1$ by its construction in step 4. The inverse maps agree as well. Apply the morphism-gluing clause of [lem-pe-set-sheaf-cover-descent] to the fpqc cover $U\to S$, first to $b$ and then to $b^{-1}$. Their global composites are identities because their restrictions are identities and that same clause gives uniqueness. Hence $H\simeq F$. Restricting to $V$ gives $F|_V\simeq h_Q$. Step 2 supplies flatness, surjectivity and finite presentation of $V\to S$, and step 5 supplies finite presentation of $Q\to V$, exactly the required conclusion.

source.place: Tag 04TQ, lemma-glue-maps, applied to b and its inverse on the original cover U to S
